title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks
content_md: Ivanti released security updates to patch two more Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1. Threat actors exploited these two flaws (tracked as CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 ) alongside an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-104935), which Ivanti patched last month to remove the main attack surface. CVE-2026-111357 is a high-severity privilege escalation flaw, and CVE-2026-118527 lets authenticated attackers upload files on an unpatched device. When it released patches for CVE-2026-104935 in October, Ivanti urged admins to upgrade as soon as possible since it was aware of "limited exploitation in the wild." "At the time of discovery of exploitation, Ivanti had a fix developed for CVE-2026-104935 which was already in QA for supported versions, and we made the decision to not delay getting a fix to customers that resolved the primary exploitation path when the LPE was discovered," Ivanti added in an advisory updated on Thursday. "Because of this, our focus was initially centered on the disclosure of CVE-2026-104935 and providing protection for our customers as quickly as possible." Cybersecurity firm Volexity, which found the flaw, reported at the time that a threat actor (UTA0576) was chaining the CVE-2026-104935 vulnerability since at least October 3 with two other flaws to gain unauthenticated root-level code execution on fully patched ICS devices.
